narrative: Amazon's Leo service has achieved sufficient satellite deployment to rival Starlink, signaling increased competition in low-Earth orbit internet. Meanwhile, Google faces a significant setback with a record EU antitrust fine over Android, highlighting ongoing regulatory challenges for tech giants. In the AI sector, NVIDIA is expanding its compute infrastructure, inviting partners to accelerate AI development, while Apple is rumored to be preparing new iPad Pro and MacBook Pro releases for early next year.

highlights.title: Amazon has enough satellites to launch its Starlink competitor
highlights.whyItMatters: Amazon's Leo service now has enough satellites for continuous service across initial latitudes, intensifying competition in space-based internet.

highlights.title: Google loses fight over record $4.7B EU antitrust fine
highlights.whyItMatters: Google's appeal against a significant EU antitrust fine has failed, underscoring regulatory pressures on its Android business practices.

highlights.title: Indian tech tycoon bets $30M of his own money to build AI alternative to Microsoft Office
highlights.whyItMatters: A new venture is aiming to challenge established office software with an AI-driven alternative, potentially disrupting the productivity suite market.

highlights.title: Kimi K2.7 Code is generally available in GitHub Copilot
highlights.whyItMatters: GitHub Copilot integrates Kimi K2.7 Code, enhancing AI-assisted development capabilities for programmers.

highlights.title: NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout
highlights.whyItMatters: NVIDIA is expanding its AI compute infrastructure, fostering partnerships to meet accelerating demand for AI production inference.

highlights.title: A new Android malware from Google
highlights.whyItMatters: A new Android malware reportedly from Google raises concerns about mobile security and app ecosystem integrity.

highlights.title: Oomwoo, an open-source robot vacuum you build yourself
highlights.whyItMatters: Oomwoo offers an open-source robotic vacuum, promoting DIY robotics and community-driven innovation in home automation.

highlights.whyItMatters: NASA provides skywatching tips for July 2026, including planetary meetups, a comet, and opportunities to view the Milky Way.
